text: AD 66. Judea rises against Rome. Legions march south. By later tradition, the believers of Jerusalem remembered his words, left the city, and crossed the Jordan to Pella.
You were trained in those courts. The place where you learned to pray is gone.
You leave with them. You lock a door you will never open again, and you do not look back until the ridge, and then you do.
You were a young scribe then. You thought: no one could throw down stones like those.
AD 70. Titus surrounds the city at Passover, when it is crowded with pilgrims. The siege lasts through the summer. Hunger does what the legions cannot. In late summer the Temple burns.
This was your uncle’s city, and yours. The place where you learned to pray is gone.

Months later you climb the Mount of Olives one last time. Where the Temple stood there is smoke-blackened rubble. The great stones lie in heaps at the foot of the platform, exactly where the soldiers levered them over.
You were a girl then. You thought: no one could throw down stones like those.

You are old now, and you remember a spring day forty years ago. The Temple stood across the valley, white and gold, so bright in the sun you could hardly look at it. Someone said how beautiful the stones were.
“Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one.” Your voice is the only sound on the hill. It is still true.
Everything he said about this place has happened. You open your scroll, there on the hill, and find the page where you wrote it down forty years ago in a young hand.
You sit down in the dust where he once wept over this city, and you weep over it too.

As some were talking about the temple and how it was decorated with beautiful stones and gifts, he said, “As for these things which you see, the days will come, in which there will not be left here one stone on another that will not be thrown down.”

“But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation is at hand. Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains. Let those who are in the midst of her depart. Let those who are in the country not enter therein.

For these are days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled. Woe to those who are pregnant and to those who nurse infants in those days! For there will be great distress in the land, and wrath to this people. They will fall by the edge of the sword, and will be led captive into all the nations. Jerusalem will be trampled down by the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will by no means pass away.
But when these things begin to happen, look up, and lift up your heads, because your redemption is near.”
